issues.title: Bundle: fallback block reuse cache + large perfect HA v3
issues.hypothesis: Two mechanisms that were each retired on acceptance alone, not on correctness. (1) The r14 fallback block cache: a bounded 64MB queue of freed 256KB blocks in BlockAllocator when block_allocator_memory=0. It fixed the warm-state slowdown of the big radix agg in-process (agg 550-714 -> 460-475ms, q18 warm 630-720 -> 500-518ms). In the bench, join templates gained (q04 -5..-12%, q07 -9% in 2 of 3 runs, q03 -12%, q05 -6..-9%), but no single template cleared its noise threshold. (2) E0013 large perfect HA (22 bits, striped combine, parallel source, lazy init, DELIM guard, buffer-allocator tables) gave q13 -17..-23% in 10 of 10 runs, clearing q13's 14% threshold. It was retired only because q18 was +8.7% in full-bench runs, and that +8.7% matches the warm-state jemalloc churn that (1) removes: q18 after q09 was ~620ms in both builds, and the slowdown was not reproducible in subsets. Together: q13 clears its threshold, the cache neutralizes the q18 artifact, and the join templates add geomean.
issues.plan: (a) Re-apply the r14 change in src/storage/block_allocator.cpp plus its header. When the pool is unused, keep a bounded 64MB queue of freed block_size allocations in AllocateData/FreeData. Drain it in ThreadFlush, FlushAll and ~BlockAllocator. (b) Re-apply E0013 as recorded in the ledger. plan_aggregate.cpp CanUsePerfectHashAggregate accepts up to 22 bits when perfect_ht_threshold >= 12, with guards: density est_input >= slots/2, memory slots*(state+1)*(threads+1) <= max_memory/8, and no DELIM_SCAN in the input subtree. Set the is_large flag. In physical_perfecthash_aggregate.cpp, large mode only: lazy per-slot InitializeStates, striped-lock Combine, block-parallel source, tables from the buffer allocator. Non-large paths stay byte-identical. Before the bench, check in one dbe-tool sql process: q09; q13; q18 x3, then the same with SET perfect_ht_threshold=11. q18 must not regress.
issues.expected_gain: q13 -17..-23%. q04/q05/q07/q03 -5..-10% (noisy). q18 neutral or slightly faster. Geomean about -3..-4%.
issues.generality: The block cache helps any query that churns 256KB buffer blocks (HJ builds, aggs, sorts) while many base-table blocks are resident, which is typical for long-lived processes. Large perfect HA helps GROUP BY on dense integer FK keys up to a 4M range with many rows per group. Risk of slowdown: sparse inputs with overestimated cardinality, measured +60% on a 1.8M-row/2M-slot case. The cache holds up to 64MB more memory.
issues.risk: Medium. Large perfect HA regressed q18 twice before, but that matches the artifact the cache fixes. The cache must be drained on memory pressure, which FlushAll does.

## Memory (gen2)

## State
- gen1 (r1-r16): accepted E0001 JoinDependent rule order (q19), E0002 contains() selectivity (q09), E0003 perfect HJ RIGHT (q13), E0005 BF first key multi-key HJ (q09), E0006 key-set range filter through compress projs (q18), E0007 exact bitmap BF, E0011 semi-join estimate, E0012 OR-of-ranges mask, E0014 FSST simple decode + substring prefilter (q13), E0016 DELIM_GET-build BF (q22 -20%). Best 1.281x.
- gen2 r1+r2: E0017/E0018 (no CM on hash-join keys) RETIRED twice: hidden validation regressed. DEAD.
- gen2 r5: E0021 = E0019 (deliminate SEMI) + E0020 (exact BF through CM offset) ACCEPTED.
- gen2 r6: E0022 exact-BF small-range floor ACCEPTED (-9.9%).
- gen2 r7: E0023 ANTI deliminator ACCEPTED.
- gen2 r8: E0024 parallel perfect-HJ build + INNER dense <=4M ACCEPTED.
- gen2 r11: E0027 BitPacking per-value select + exact BF to 2^27 ACCEPTED.
- gen2 r13: E0029 = E0028 sparse perfect-HJ exact BF + fixed 8-byte BitPacking extract ACCEPTED (-2.5%). Best 1.719x.
- gen2 r14: fallback block cache (64MB reuse queue in BlockAllocator) RETIRED: geomean -1.6%, but no template beyond noise. q04 -5..-12%, q07 -9%, q03 -12%, q05 -6..-9%. In bench, q18 is already in the fast state (~530ms).
- gen2 r15: DISPATCHED bundle "fallback block reuse cache + large perfect HA v3" (q13 -20% from E0013 should clear its threshold; the cache should neutralize the q18 full-bench artifact).
- Claude auto-memory (~/.claude/.../memory) holds results from a PREVIOUS evolve run. Treat them as strong priors.

## Resident-memory agg slowdown (r14, root cause found)
- Cause: jemalloc per-block alloc/free of 256KB blocks gets slow once arenas are shared with many long-lived base-table blocks. It is not decay/purge, not TLB/THP, not reservations, not eviction queues.
- Fixes: block_allocator_memory pool, or a small (16-64 block) reuse cache. A 64MB cache was implemented in block_allocator.cpp AllocateData/FreeData, drained in ThreadFlush/FlushAll/dtor.
- read_csv can read /sys files; /proc reads as empty.

## Acceptance lessons
- Acceptance needs BOTH: some template faster beyond its noise AND a visible geomean that improves. Any template slower beyond noise gets the issue retired.
- Bundle a near-miss with a general second mechanism hitting the SAME template (worked in E0021, E0027, E0029). r15 bundles the near-miss with the fix for its blocker instead.

## Measured r14
- q09 plan: HJ o_orderkey=l_orderkey 1.37s CPU (build 3.27M lineitem side, probe 2.94M orders); lineitem scan 3.57s CPU; HJ partkey/suppkey 0.61s; part contains scan 0.33s.
- q13 orders scan: FSST decode ~95ms wall; 'packages' search adds ~50ms.

## Key finding r13: q07
- HJ o_orderkey=l_orderkey 0.48s CPU builds 1.46M rows (wide payload) and probes 100k. Build is superlinear (330ns/row). Flipping does not help.
- Scan filters already use AdaptiveFilter (row_group.cpp:759).

## Codebase facts
- Perfect HJ BF: CanUseBloomFilter + PushPerfectHashJoinBloomFilters (physical_hash_join.cpp); PerfectHashJoinExecutor::FillExactBloomFilter.
- BitPacking: bitpacking.cpp (Select ~886, per-value when sel*4<=count). DELTA_FOR still decodes everything.
- TEMP tables are never compressed.
- Substring prefilter: column_segment.cpp:662-860.
- Radix agg memory: radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp GetThreadLimit :163. BlockAllocator: block_allocator.cpp.
- CM: src/optimizer/compressed_materialization*. Deliminator: deliminator.cpp. Join filters: join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp. Perfect HA: plan_aggregate.cpp + physical_perfecthash_aggregate.cpp.

## How to measure
- Micro A/B: CREATE TEMP VIEW a/b; alternate them in one dbe-tool sql call (each call is a new process).
- Full operator timings: SET enable_profiling='json'; profiling_output under the slot's .dbe/.
- Bench noise thresholds: q16 ~7.9%, q18 ~5%, q13 ~14%, q09 ~8.6%, q14 ~5.1%, q05 ~20%, q04 ~20%, q07 ~13%.

## Profile snapshot (r15): q18 542, q13 524, q09 405, q05 185, q16 175, q03 172, q07 169, q04 161, q08 153, q14 115, q17 115, q19 111, q22 106, q02 57. Geomean 174.2.

## Dead / exhausted
- CM join-key removal, HJ prefetch, agg run-collapse, in-place finalize, FSST heap reuse, dictionary filter, scan filter cost ordering, early HT grow, sparse perfect HJ (8M range), hashed BF through CM offset, q13 eager aggregation, fused hashed BF probe, CM fold decompress/compress, allocator flush thresholds.

## Next candidates (round 16)
1. If the r15 bundle fails on q18 again: the q18 artifact is not jemalloc, so drop large perfect HA for good.
2. If it fails only on noise: re-bundle the block cache with the substring search speedup (q13), or try DELTA_FOR select.
3. Large HJ builds (q09 1.37s, q07 0.48s): a partitioned build is too big for one round.
